title: On a Noetherian scheme a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules embeds into a finite sum of finite pushforwards of constant sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring and $F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an object of $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then there are an integer $n\ge0$ and, for $i=1,\dots,n$, a finite morphism $f_i:Y_i\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and a finite $\Lambda$-module $M_i$, and a monomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $F\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^nf_{i,*}\underline{M_i}$ into the finite direct sum (biproduct [def-weil-additive-category]) in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, where $\underline{M_i}$ is the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with value $M_i$ on $Y_{i,\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $f_{i,*}$ the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. (Stacks states this for Noetherian $\Lambda$, and adds that the $Y_i$ may be taken integral, finite over integral closed subschemes $Z_i$ and finite etale over a nonempty open of $Z_i$; that addition is not part of this node.)

proof.text: *Setup at a point; the generic trivialization.* Fix a point $x\in X$ and let $\varepsilon_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ be the canonical morphism. The inverse image $\varepsilon_x^{-1}F$ is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ by [prop-constructible-pullback] (on the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ every stratum is trivially a constructible subset, so condition (a) of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] holds). By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-field-finite-separable-constant] there are a finite separable extension $K/\kappa(x)$, a finite $\Lambda$-module $M$ and an isomorphism $\pi^{-1}\varepsilon_x^{-1}F\cong\underline M_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. Put $h=\varepsilon_x\circ\pi:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$; composing with the canonical isomorphism $h^{-1}\cong\pi^{-1}\varepsilon_x^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] gives an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules $\alpha:h^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline M_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$. (Stacks: 'Since $\mathcal F$ is constructible, there is a finite separable extension $K/\kappa(x)$ such that $\mathcal F|_{\Spec(K)}$ is the constant sheaf with value $E$'.)

*The normal model.* $X$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] applied to $x$ and $K/\kappa(x)$ there are a normal integral scheme $Y$, an integral morphism $\nu:Y\to X$ and the inclusion $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ of the generic point of $Y$ (with $K$ as function field) such that $h=\nu\circ g$. (Stacks takes the normalization of the reduced closure $Z=\overline{\{x\}}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and composes with $Z\to X$; that is the same $X$-scheme, by the last clause of Stacks 035I, recorded in the new node; working over $X$ directly removes the closed immersion from the argument.)

u_*\underline M$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic] applied to the normal integral $Y$ and $g$, the unit $u:\underline M_Y	o g_*g^{-1}\underline M_Y$ is an isomorphism; the node is stated for a finite abelian group $E$, and $M$ is one; $u$ is the unit of the adjunction $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, which is $\Lambda$-linear by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-adjunction], so $u$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules (the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules has the constant abelian sheaf as underlying sheaf, both being sheafifications of the same presheaf, [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]); and $g^{-1}\underline M_Y\cong\underline M_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$ by [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. proof.text:
*$\varphi$ is injective at every geometric point over $x$.* Let $ ar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o X$ be a geometric point lying over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], i.e. a field map $\kappa(x)	o\Omega$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. As $K/\kappa(x)$ is algebraic it extends to $K	o\Omega$, giving a geometric point $ ar\omega$ of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $h\circ ar\omega= ar x$; put $ ar y=g\circ ar\omega$, so $
u\circ ar y= ar x$. (i) $g^{-1}(\psi)$ equals $\alpha'$ up to the identification $g^{-1}\underline M_Y=\underline M_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$: indeed $\varepsilon_g\circ g^{-1}(u)=\mathrm{id}$ (triangle identity, $u$ being the unit at $\underline M_Y$) and $g^{-1}(u)$ is an isomorphism, so $g^{-1}(u)^{-1}=\varepsilon_g$, whence $g^{-1}\psi=\varepsilon_g\circ g^{-1}g_*(\alpha')\circ g^{-1}(\eta_g)=\alpha'\circ\varepsilon_g\circ g^{-1}(\eta_g)=\alpha'$ by naturality of $\varepsilon_g$ and the other triangle identity. By the natural isomorphism $c_{g, ar\omega}:(g^{-1}H)_{ ar\omega}\cong H_{ ar y}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] (natural in $H$), $\psi_{ ar y}$ corresponds to $(g^{-1}\psi)_{ ar\omega}=\alpha'_{ ar\omega}$, an isomorphism. (ii) Let $r:(
u_*\underline M_Y)_{ ar x}	o(\underline M_Y)_{ ar y}$ be the restriction map of [lem-weil-pbc-counit-stalk-germ-restriction] and $c=c_{
u, ar y,F}:(
u^{-1}F)_{ ar y}\cong F_{ ar x}$. Since $\psi=\varepsilon_
u\circ
u^{-1}(\varphi)$, $(\varepsilon_
u)_{ ar y}=r\circ c$ ([lem-weil-pbc-counit-stalk-germ-restriction]) and $c\circ(
u^{-1}\varphi)_{ ar y}=\varphi_{ ar x}\circ c$ (naturality of $c$), we get $\psi_{ ar y}=r\circ\varphi_{ ar x}\circ c$. By (i) the left side is bijective, so $\varphi_{ ar x}$ is injective. This is Stacks' commutative square $\mathcal F_{ ar x}=(\mathcal F|_Y)_{ ar y}	o\underline E_{ ar y}$ through $(f_*\underline E)_{ ar x}$, written out.

proof.text: *Finitely many points suffice.* Choose for every $x\in X$ data $(f_x,M_x,\varphi_x)$ as in the previous steps. Every geometric point of $X$ lies over some $x$, and there $\varphi_x$ is injective on stalks. The underlying abelian sheaf of $F$ is a constructible abelian sheaf (the same stratification serves: a constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with finite value is, as an abelian sheaf, constant with finite value; [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]). By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-noetherian-finite-selection], applied on the Noetherian scheme $X$ to the family $(\varphi_x)_{x\in X}$ of maps of abelian sheaves, there is a finite set $\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subseteq X$ such that $(\varphi_{x_k})_k:F\to\bigoplus_{k=1}^nf_{x_k,*}\underline{M_{x_k}}$ is a monomorphism of abelian sheaves. The finite direct sum in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ is the biproduct [def-weil-additive-category] whose underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian direct sum (sectionwise product with componentwise $\Lambda$-action), and the map is $\Lambda$-linear, each component being so; the forgetful functor $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is faithful, hence reflects monomorphisms, so the map is a monomorphism in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. With $f_k=f_{x_k}$, $Y_k=Y_{x_k}$, $M_k=M_{x_k}$ this is the assertion (for $X=\emptyset$, $n=0$). REMARK on the source: Stacks deduces this step from the ascending chain condition of Lemma 09YV ('Because we have the ascending chain condition for subsheaves of $\mathcal F$ ... it suffices to show that for every point $x$ ...'). As written that inference does not go through: the kernels $\ker(F\to\bigoplus_{x\in S}f_{x,*}\underline{M_x})$ for growing finite $S$ form a descending family, and constructible sheaves do not satisfy the descending chain condition (on $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/2$, the subsheaves $j_{n!}\underline{\Lambda}\subset\underline\Lambda$, $j_n$ the inclusion of the complement of the first $n$ primes, descend strictly). The step therefore follows the alternative that Stacks gives in the same sentence ('This argument can be avoided by picking a partition of $X$ as in Lemma 095E and constructing a $Y_i\to X$ for each irreducible component of each part'), which is the proof of [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-noetherian-finite-selection]; this is below the unit level and keeps the unit's route.

reviewed.note: Eight steps along Stacks 09Z6 (1), carried to the module form (3): the generic trivialization at a point (new node lem-weil-pbc-constructible-field-finite-separable-constant), the normal model (new node lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension, 035I), the map F -> nu_* M via lem-weil-pbc-normal-constant-generic (09Z5) and the module adjunction, injectivity at geometric points over x (triangle identities, stalk-germ leaves), Y as a limit of finite X-schemes (new node lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite, 09YZ/0817), nu_* M as the colimit of finite pushforwards (tool use sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-limit, 09Z1 in degree 0), factorization through a finite stage by lem-weil-pbc-constructible-finitely-presented (09Z4; the only place where Lambda Noetherian enters), finitely many points (tool use lem-weil-pbc-constructible-noetherian-finite-selection; see the literature note). LITERATURE NOTE (worker, recorded in STATE): Stacks 09Z6 justifies 'finitely many points suffice' by the ACC 09YV, which does not apply to the shrinking kernels (no DCC: on Spec Z with Lambda = Z/2 the extensions by zero from complements of more and more primes form a strictly descending chain); the step uses the partition alternative Stacks mentions in the same sentence. The attached Lean takes any CommRing Lambda (no finiteness), stronger than the node; the IsConstructibleSheaf defect is harmless on a Noetherian scheme.
